newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ survey respondents see some further easing.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ survey respondents see some further easing.

text.p: New Zealand monetary conditions are perceived to have loosened since November, according to the Reserve Bank's latest Survey of Expectations, released on Wednesday.

However, a net 54 percent of respondents in the RBNZ's February survey believe conditions are still tighter than neutral, down from 63 percent in November and 89 percent in August. Respondents anticipate monetary conditions will have eased further by the end of June, with a net 46 percent expecting conditions to be tighter than neutral by that time.
The results represent the views of respondents in the financial, business, farming and labour branches of the economy, not those of the bank.

Respondents expect headline inflation of 0.5 percent in the March quarter (up from 0.4 percent in the previous survey), and 0.4 percent in the June quarter. For the year to December, CPI inflation is expected to be 1.9 percent, compared with a 1.8 percent one-year-ahead expectation recorded in November.
Underlying inflation was anticipated at 1.7 percent for the year to December, and to have risen to 1.8 percent for the year to December 1998, unchanged from the previous survey.

The RBNZ said survey respondents expected a small rise in interest rates this year. They picked the 90-day bill rate at 7.5 percent at the end of March, a little lower than the rate prevailing when the survey was completed. Respondents expected that by the end of December the 90-day rate would have risen to 7.6 percent.
Ten-year government security yields were picked at 7.5 percent by the end of December, implying an expected negative yield gap of 0.1 percentage points.
The currency's Trade-Weighted Index, at 68.4 when the survey was taken, was expected to fall to 67.6 by the end of June and 67.3 by the end of December.
Real GDP was expected to have risen by 0.5 percent in the December 1996 and March 1997 quarters, largely unchanged from the November survey.
A government surplus of NZ$2.3 billion was expected for the year to June, compared with $2.5 billion in the previous survey.

The current account deficit for the year ended March 1997 was expected to be $3.8 billion. This was up from the $3.4 billion expectation for the year to December recorded in the last survey, but lower than the latest outturn of $4.2 billion.
Unemployment, which stood at 5.9 percent in the December 1996 quarter, was expected to rise to 6.4 percent in the December 1997 quarter, and to drop to 6.3 percent by the December 1998 quarter.
The RBNZ survey, conducted on February 12, canvassed 250 respondents and attracted a response rate of 56 percent.
